blocked_layers: Existing guards entry requires named real-DTS rejection of an invalid second element, negative ID and 65536 before uint16_t narrowing; positive first/last IDs, empty and omitted lists remain accepted. All three missing-rejection regressions fail before repair; prior guards and runtime init checks are retained.
preserved_assertions: Relocated fixtures retain their prior assertions; no snapshot auto-accept or unique assertion removal.

execution.quick: All behavioral scenarios once; sanitizer variants where supported.
execution.full: Same scenarios plus relevant optimization, ABI, role, kernel and supported-core checks.
execution.outputs: Use a fresh evidence directory; existing evidence is never overwritten.
execution.coverage: Every gated real function range requires measured executable lines. The actual full entry rejects empty, unrelated and partial synthetic reports; normal full runs retain actual line/branch measurement and existing behavioral assertions. Macro expansions are measured in their callers.

gaps: Physical USB/BLE/split delivery, timing, power and retention require matching production-board evidence.
suppression_scope: No button-pair/final-frame policy is owned here. Existing transform/layer/settings fixtures remain unchanged; AKKB relative-motion configuration composes with an independent final filter.
scheduled_work_settings_review: All four adapters now dispatch a changed descriptor only to its owning instance; initialization still applies every instance. The host bridge stand-in carries descriptor identity and covers foreign events and every own field. The DYA settings fixture uses the actual registry and worker queue: foreign-subsystem, same-subsystem scaler and peer-layer edits must preserve queued activation and the original idle deadline. Every write changes its value so notification suppression cannot hide this regression. Its snapshot adds the named unrelated-edit scenario; all prior lines remain. Direct temporary-layer API setters retain their documented reset behavior.
concurrent_settings: Each adapter serializes its complete registry read/apply transaction. The real DYA settings fixture pauses a read in writer A, commits writer B from a higher priority Zephyr thread, and verifies that the older snapshot cannot win. This adds a second named settings scenario; all old snapshot lines remain. Linker wrapping controls the real registry boundary only in the owner test module.
selected_workspace: Workspace selection uses tests/integration/workspace-env.sh to export the selected manifest's ZEPHYR_MODULES and explicit Zephyr package/base paths. A Zephyr symlink to a different cache must not select that cache's module providers. The owner test_workspace_env.py exercises actual selection with a poisoned ambient list, a cache symlink, module paths containing spaces, failed project discovery and an empty selection. The keep-ambient negative control must fail these assertions. Full integration retains all supported-core, role, persistence and invalid-DTS cases. No dependency is patched or required feature disabled.

integer_width.production: 32-bit arithmetic; independent wider oracles remain test-only
integer_width.contract: Scaler products, fractions and saturated results use checked 32-bit arithmetic, including the full int32 input range. Layer clocks use uint32 milliseconds and explicit pending-deadline state, so a deadline of zero after wrap is valid. Half-range deadline ordering assumes delays/observations below 2^31 ms; long silent spans can be ambiguous. The typing guard conservatively suppresses a timestamp interpreted as future.
integer_width.fixtures: Scalar: test_scaler.c independent wide reference, signed extremes, stale fractions, zero/identity and saturation; test_scaler_width.py rejects wide helpers in a 32-bit object. Layer: test_temp_layer_policy.c and runtime/temp_layer_harness.c retain guards/deadlines and add modulo-clock wrap/zero-deadline cases.
integer_width.timeout_boundary: Three reservations use exact native32 timeout division; public0..60000 and fulluint32 remaining duration, tick ABI, clock wrap and cancellation preserved. Host exhaustive bounds/width/fault controls and real Zephyr comparison inside unchanged native snapshots. Physical timing unmeasured.

raw_event_abi_guards.asserts: Raw event ABI DTS guards: the actual CMake/owner-object path rejects type -1/256 on all three drivers and every x-codes/y-codes/codes/map first, second and last entry at -1/65536. Fourteen named fixtures include all list elements, not only index zero. Shared positive nodes compile type0/255, code0/65535, omitted type (default REL) and empty lists. Transform equal lengths and mapper pair counts remain unchanged. Before repair all14 malformed fixtures build on both stock and DYA; no snapshot or runtime assertion is weakened. Default guards retain all15 existing cases and add14; configure/build proceeds one case at a time. Stock raw-event checks select only these14 common fixtures; the existing Studio name-length fixtures remain DYA-only. Optional explicit guard case names select a focused run; the default canonical integration always runs all29 on DYA.

arithmetic_fast_paths.contract: For ratios 1/1 and 0/1, the scaler clears any carried fraction and returns the unchanged input or zero before generic multiplication/division. Other identity/zero ratios retain their signed fraction semantics. tests/cost/scaler_fastpath.c checks signed endpoints, every int16 carried value, null remainder, larger-divisor counterexamples and zero checked products in the actual header. The canonical quick/full entry includes this fixture. This operation count is not a CPU-cycle or physical HID measurement.
